On 24 April, Olly Foote (8.17.3) and Dave North (8.26.5) ran pb's over 3000m while Mike Hayes placed 2nd in the 'chase in 9.03.9, also a fine pb; Phil Lovell won the Pole Vault at 4.80 and Ken Onuaguluchi placed 2nd in the Discus with 51.34.

His 1500m time of 3.48.5 is 0.1 faster than John Bicourts p.b. and as John has been advising Mark on hurdling technique it is pleasing to see Mark move to 3rd spot on our all time 3000s/c rankings with a fine 8.56.9. Our strength in this event is considerable with Mike Hayes close to a sub 9.00 effort.
Fortunately Gary Staines, Mike Hayes and Martin Lake were on good form and we ended up 4th in the League with Epsom and Omega due for the drop.

Oliver Foote dropped out (the start of five) but Dave North showed good form while Mike Hayes returned to competition after illness and gradually worked through the field to finish in a creditable position.
Mike Hayes again gave an indication that he is over illness as he moved steadily through while Dave North who had succumbed to 'flu the week before battled gamely through to finish.
Next on STAGE NINE came Mike Hayes with another good run to push us back up to sixth. STAGE TEN saw another newcomer to our team Richard O'Hara with a good stint to maintain our position.
Mark Sinclair was another to smash his previous best, as a sparkling 8.44.88 gave him 6th place in the 'chase with Mike Hayes also under 9 minutes in the heats.

In the Triple Jump, Derek Browne bounded out to another pb of 14.77, the first time he had used a 15 stride approach instead of 9, and that obviously worked, while Mike Hayes was a creditable 9th in the steeplechase with 8.53.16.

Twelve wins were again recorded and included Gary Staines running away from Dave Baptiste, Phil Goedluck, Mark Sinclair, Derrick Williams (Long and Triple), Ken and Abi in the Discus, Phil Lovell and Mike Hayes and Simon Maynard in the Chase.
